summary: Oxford County, ME steel fire tower on Pleasant Mountain, erected 1920 at 48 ft in Denmark; standing, now described as boarded up.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower, 48 ft in 1920; glass-enclosed cab at the summit (Secret Falls trail page)
facts.status_note: Described as boarded up (Press Herald); FFLA lists it as standing without the asterisk used for towers that have lost their cabs

staffing.status: manned through the summer season in 1939 (Bath Independent); no current staffing found

access.note: Summit trails are open for four-season hiking (Press Herald); the tower is described as boarded up, so climbing it is not confirmed

visit.trail_note: Ledges Trail, 1.8 miles, the shortest and most popular route up the eastern side; trail network managed by Loon Echo Land Trust

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA list, Forest Lookouts and Digital Maine say Oxford County; the Secret Falls trail page says Cumberland County. The Press Herald says the mountain spans the Bridgton-Denmark line. Recorded as Oxford County, matching the record and the majority of sources.

notes_for_editor: Current cab and tower condition is unresolved: FFLA gives no asterisk (cab presumed in place), the Press Herald says boarded up, and Secret Falls describes a glass cab in present tense. A search summary said the tower was lowered to 36 ft in 1960 and that the Maine towers were abandoned by the 1960s; neither was verified in a page read, so both are left out. A Conway Daily Sun article on a replica map stand returned HTTP 429 and was not read. Search summary ownership figures (Loon Echo about 2,000 acres, TNC 1,400 acres, Maine Forest Service 20 acres) were not verified and are not used. The OpenStreetMap way was not read. The Press Herald article's date was not shown in the text read, so it is not cited by date. Brief height_m 20.0 is proposed for removal (see corrections).
